content:
Apple's annual major launch event will be held this Wednesday, when three brand new iPhone models will be unveiled: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Below is a preview of the event.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will follow up on the hugely popular iPhone 17 Pro series.

Rumoured new features include:

  • A20 Pro chip, delivering stronger performance and better power efficiency
  • A major camera system upgrade, with the main camera adding a variable aperture
  • Dynamic Island reduced by 35% for a more modern design
  • A new colour option, with bold wine red as the headline shade
  • All-time best battery life, with the iPhone 18 Pro Max seeing significant improvement
  • Redesigned Camera Control button
  • Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem
  • New satellite features, including 5G satellite connectivity

The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to see a higher starting price. External estimates put it at around US$1,399, but I think it will be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is believed to be the name of Apple's first foldable-screen phone, with an expected price tag exceeding US$2,000, creating an entirely new premium market segment.

It adopts a book-style wide foldable design, with an outer display of approximately 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches, delivering an experience similar to an iPad mini.

The body materials are expected to follow the iPhone Air, featuring a titanium frame for a slim and sleek design.

The iPhone Ultra will feature two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide) and two front cameras, one for each display. Authentication will switch from Face ID to Touch ID.

The software experience will be the biggest highlight of this device. Paired with iOS 27, it supports split-screen multitasking and adaptive landscape layout, fully leveraging the advantages of the new form factor.

Performance is expected to be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, also powered by the A20 Pro chip, and equipped with a vapour chamber cooling system and C2 modem.

Missing models: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

As usual, the September event typically sees the simultaneous launch of a new entry-level iPhone 18 and the successor to the iPhone Air.

However, reports suggest Apple will significantly adjust its autumn product lineup this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It remains unclear whether this arrangement is purely a strategic decision or driven by current memory supply constraints. Regardless of the reason, this autumn's new iPhone lineup will focus exclusively on the high-end market, with no more affordable options.

Are you planning to upgrade to a new iPhone this autumn? Which model has caught your eye? Let us know in the comments.
